author: Unreal Engine
description:
Epic Games’ Matt Oztalay can talk about how to get your project running at your target frame rate until he’s hoarse (and in fact has!). Wouldn’t it be better for you—and Matt’s vocal cords—if you started your project at your target frame rate and kept it that way? 

In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Chicago 2026, Matt takes a journey through Unreal Engine 5’s development to see how Epic has been improving performance of the engine; the tools you need to build your project at your target frame rate from the ground up; the features and tools to monitor and diagnose your project’s performance; and how you can get back to frame rate if (but hopefully not when) you get off track.

Find out about using Unreal Engine to develop games here: unrealengine.com/uses/games

Check out the Epic Developer Community article here: https://dev.epicgames.com/community/learning/talks-and-demos/YoB7/unreal-engine-how-to-start-your-project-at-60-fps-and-keep-it-there

#FrameRateOptimization, #60FPS, #
title: How to Start Your Project at 60 FPS and Keep It There | Unreal Fest Chicago 2026

author: Unreal Engine
description:
This recording of a session presented by Unknown Worlds at Unreal Fest Chicago 2026 covers some of the many lessons learned during the development of ‘Subnautica 2’: a large, open world, multiplayer game in UE5. 

Offering insights from the experience of making a multiplayer game with over 100,000 actors and a map many miles by many miles, the team makes a quick stop at each issue, explaining the problem they faced, the solutions they tried—and often, the solution they didn't try but should have. 

The talk covers the performance of a large world—especially in multiplayer—including both at runtime and in editor, using all the latest UE5 tools and techniques such as World Partition, One File Per Actor, Level Instances, Foliage, PCG, and Nanite. 

There is  also a discussion on how to know when you should roll your own tools and when you should use the inbuilt tools in Unreal Engine, with examples of situations where the team got it right and some situations where they got it wrong.

title: Lessons Learned from Building a Very Large Open World Game in UE5 | Unreal Fest Chicago 2026
